newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier close to de Havilland deal.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier close to de Havilland deal.

text.p: Bombardier Inc Chief Executive Officer Laurent Beaudoin said on Monday that the Quebec-based aerospace and transportation conglomerate expects to close a deal to purchase the rest of its majority owned de Havilland unit from the Ontario government by the end of January.
"I think we'll get a deal resolved before the expiry date for our agreement which is for the end of January," he told reporters after a speech in Toronto.
Beaudoin said Bombardier expects to buy 49 percent of de Havilland from Ontario for C$49 million.
"I think the price is not an issue," he said.
Beaudoin also said Bombardier had a firm book of 60 orders for its new Global Express jet.
"We mentioned two weeks ago in Orlando that our firm book order (for Global Express planes) is close to 60 orders," he said.
He said Bombardier plans to invest C$600 million in its Canadair unit if it decides to launch the 70-seat CRJ-X jet.

He also mentioned that Bombardier was producing 10 Neighborhood Electric Vehicles (NEV) a day. He said orders for them already exceeded production, but the company would wait a year to see whether to increase production.
Bombardier shares were up C$1.20 a share at C$24.25 on volume of 1,360 shares traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The Quebec firm builds planes, railway cars, military defence equipment, snowmobiles and jet-powered boats.
